question: On 15 May 2025, the Supreme Court of India issued an immediate direction to the Centre to set up dedicated courts to deal with which cases?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Child sexual abuse**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Child sexual abuse** is a heinous crime involving exploitation or harm to minors for sexual purposes. It can include a wide range of offenses, including molestation, rape, and child pornography.
 
• To combat this issue, the **Supreme Court of India** directed the establishment of dedicated courts to expedite justice for victims and ensure sensitive handling of cases.
 
• This decision aligns with the provisions of the **Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act, 2012**, which was enacted to safeguard children against sexual offenses and provide a child-friendly judicial process. *Hence, the direction is significant in addressing these crimes.*
 
• The Supreme Court's directive aims to ensure timely justice and reduce the trauma for child victims during legal proceedings. Dedicated courts will also focus on creating a safe environment for children during trials.
 
• The establishment of specialized courts also seeks to address the high pendency rate of child sexual abuse cases and ensure that perpetrators are brought to justice efficiently and effectively. *Hence, the correct answer is Child sexual abuse.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act, 2012:**

 
 
• This act is a comprehensive law enacted by the Indian Government to protect children (**below the age of 18 years**) from sexual assault, harassment, and pornography.
 
• The act provides for a **child-friendly judicial procedure**, ensuring that the dignity and rights of the child are preserved during legal processes. It mandates the establishment of **Special Courts** for speedy trial of such offenses.
 
• It prescribes stringent punishment for offenses, including imprisonment ranging from **20 years to life imprisonment**, depending on the severity of the crime.
 
 
 
• **Role of the Supreme Court in Addressing Child Sexual Abuse:**
 
 
• The **Supreme Court** plays a pivotal role in directing the government to establish mechanisms for justice delivery in sensitive cases like child sexual abuse.
 
• By mandating dedicated courts, the judiciary aims to ensure expedited justice and child-sensitive handling of cases.
 
• The court has emphasized the need for proper infrastructure, training of judicial staff, and specialized training for judges to deal with such cases effectively.
 
 
 
• **Importance of Dedicated Courts:**
 
 
• Dedicated courts help reduce the trauma experienced by child victims during trials by providing a safe environment and ensuring swift justice.
 
• They also address the issue of case backlog, ensuring speedy resolution and reducing the pendency of cases related to child sexual abuse.
 
• Specialized courts and legal frameworks contribute to creating a society where children feel protected and empowered to report offenses without fear.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Recent Developments:**

 
 
• In recent years, the Indian judiciary has taken proactive measures to address the issue of child sexual abuse. For instance, the Supreme Court has directed the government to ensure proper implementation of the POCSO Act.
 
• The Ministry of Women and Child Development has also launched initiatives to spread awareness about child rights and the legal provisions available under the POCSO Act.
 
 
 
• **Challenges:**
 
 
• Despite the legal framework, challenges such as lack of awareness, social stigma, and delays in judicial processes persist, making it difficult for victims to seek justice.
 
• Effective implementation of the Supreme Court’s directive requires adequate infrastructure, trained personnel, and public awareness campaigns to ensure the protection of child rights.
